note: The declared, reviewed list of places where this language intentionally answers differently from CPython. velocity/score.py reads this file: strict C2 counts every completed probe that disagrees with CPython, and C2_policy counts only the disagreements no entry here claims. `--gate` fails on C2_policy, so a declared divergence does not block a package and an undeclared one always does. An entry claims a probe by name or fnmatch glob in `probes`; every claimed probe must still diverge (score.py reports a claimed probe that now agrees as a stale entry). `cases` are expression/value pairs the divergence is reproducible from: velocity/divergence_evidence.py evaluates each expression under both runtimes and fails when the declared value does not reproduce. Deleting an entry, not editing one, is how a divergence stops being declared: the divergence then becomes a C2 gate failure until the language changes or a new reviewed entry replaces it.
gate_rule: score.py --gate exits 1 when a completed probe disagrees with CPython and no entry in this file claims its name; a claimed disagreement is reported but does not gate.

entries.title: round() breaks ties away from zero and answers an integral float
entries.mylang: round(value) takes a float and answers the nearest integral float with halves away from zero, matching math.round and format_float; int(round(2.5)) is 3.
entries.cpython: round(value) answers an int for a one-argument call and breaks ties to even; round(2.5) is 2, so int(round(2.5)) is 2.
documented_at: docs/python-syntax.md#builtins (round(value) answers the nearest integral float, with halves away from zero)
entries.rationale: The language's rule is deliberate and internally consistent: math.round, format_float and the SPEC bullet PRELUDE-ROUND-1 all round halves away from zero, which is C's round() and IEEE roundToIntegralTiesAway. The divergence is therefore declared, not repaired: it is a Python-fidelity hazard for an agent that writes round(x) expecting CPython's ties-to-even int, and the honest instrument reports it as such. Changing the rule is a language decision (velocity/backlog.json C-1) that this measurement package does not make.
entries.decision: keep the documented rule; report the divergence strictly and exempt it from the package gate by this declaration

review.reviewer: measurement package (WS-MEASURE); the language decision itself remains open in backlog C-1
